title: An issue or PR's own opening body claims an issue fixed that's still open
author: kothar-wa-khasis
description: Extracts every real GitHub closing-keyword claim ('fixes #N', 'closes #N', 'resolves #N', both tenses, the shared seam_engine.closing_keywords grammar) from an issue or pull request's own OPENING BODY and checks whether the named issue is actually closed. issue-comment-claims-unfixed-issue's own docstring drew this exact line and left it open on purpose: that recipe checks the ordinary TIMELINE COMMENT thread, a genuinely different GitHub object from the opening body issue-body-dangling-reference and issue-body-claims-open-milestone already watch for other claim shapes on this exact surface -- but neither of those two ever checks a closing-keyword claim against the issue tracker's own state, so the unfixed-issue leg of this surface had never actually been built anywhere until now. This recipe is the issue/PR-body-sourced sibling of issue-comment-claims-unfixed-issue, applying its identical closing-keyword grammar to the opening body instead of a timeline comment.
confidence_notes: Age-gated off the claiming record's own updated_at, the identical shape issue-body-dangling-reference, issue-body-claims-open-milestone, and issue-comment-claims-unfixed-issue already establish -- 0.55 within 24h since last update, 0.85 past it. An issue or PR body is a text surface its own author can still edit at any time, so a fresh claim earns a grace period before being scored as a confirmed gap. A claimed issue that doesn't exist at all is excluded at confidence 0.0, named not hidden -- that broken reference is issue-body-dangling-reference's own seam, not this one's (a bare #N claim and a closing-keyword #N claim name the same number space, but issue-body-dangling-reference only ever asks whether the reference resolves, never whether a closing-keyword claim about it holds -- the two recipes never collide on the same candidate). A claimed issue that IS closed is excluded too -- the claim was simply true. A body with no closing-keyword claim phrase at all, or no body at all, produces no surfaced candidate -- there is no claim to have broken. Deliberately checks only the issue list, never the PR list, the identical scope every other *-claims-unfixed-issue sibling holds itself to -- a closing-keyword claim naming a real pull request is a future issue-body-claims-unmerged-pr's own remit, not this one's.
